newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes pare gains late, diffs range bound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes pare gains late, diffs range bound.

text.p: U.S. crudes pared gains in late trade Monday after rising sharply on the back of gasoline but with differentials narrowly range bound.
December pipeline trade got off to a slow start after the completion of pipeline scheduling Friday, but with sweet grades still buoyant amid a tight arbitrage and thin supplies.
Dec West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.70-80 a barrel, up about 10 cents, with Dec/Jan backwardation widening and lending support to WTI/Cushing Posting Plus.
The spread rose five cents a barrel to 50 cents, nudging WTI/Cushing P Plus to a high of postings plus $2.24 a barrel.
The grade traded earlier today at $2.17 a barrel, gaining steadily from Friday's $2.15 level for December.

Domestic grades were mostly trapped in narrow ranges with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James trading from 65 to 70 cents premium over WTI, at parity with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire which drew refiner interest for its distillate yield.
But traders expect dwindling values for Dated Brent to soon depress the bullish trend in light domestic deltas.
"There are a few Brent sellers with supply but no firm numbers talked because the market is not keen on picking them up," a Gulf Coast trader said.
WTI/Midland was done at 5 cts over the WTI/Cushing, within the same range seen on Friday.
Sours also held steady although news Venezuela's Amuay refinery catcracker coming back on stream in three weeks was seen helping the bearish market outlook.
Traders had projected more surplus heavy sours for the U.S. Gulf, if the refinery should suffer prolonged problems.
West Texas Sour/Midland was sold at a $1.50/1.49 discount to the marker, while Eugene Island was widely pegged at $1.25-$1.05 under WTI/Cushing.

Elsewhere, a valve failure causing an upset at Amoco's huge Texas City refinery, and talk a 40,000 barrel per day gasoline unit at Chevron's Pascagoula, Mississippi refinery would undergo maintenance this week, cast a bearish pall.
While sending products higher, traders said crude demand would be tempered in the short-term.
